newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles council discusses sports complex plan.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles council discusses sports complex plan.

text.p: Los Angeles City Council met Wednesday to discuss a proposed downtown sports complex, but officials said no decisions were expected.

"Under no circumstances should Wednesday's council discussion be viewed as any final action," Los Angeles Council President John Ferraro and Councilmember Rita Walters, who chairs the Ad Hoc Committee on the Sports Arena, said in a joint statement.
"After receiving an update from the city negotiating team council members will give instructions on further negotiations," they stated.
Once the negotiation period closes and the proposed agreement is drafted, the statement said public hearings would be held before any final vote is taken.

As proposed last summer, city taxpayers would provide the land and developers would build and operate the $200 million sports complex, which would house the Kings hockey team and the Lakers basketball team.
Under the plan, the city would issue about $60.5 million of bonds to acquire and clear land for the arena at the Los Angeles Convention Center.
